parameters.content:
## Slack approvals with Block Kit
Ask a person in Slack before a workflow changes anything. The card shows Before and After, and the reviewer can Approve, Edit in a modal, Reject with a reason, or open a page for a longer list. Alerts get buttons that do the next step (Match price, Snooze, Ignore).

### How it works
1. **Setup** creates the `approvals` data table.
2. **Ask**: any workflow calls this one (lane ask). It posts the card, saves a row and returns at once, so nothing sits waiting.
3. **Click**: one Request URL takes every button. It checks Slack's signature and age, the app, team and approver list, and that the row is still pending.
4. **Apply** runs the change (your workflow, or the demo Shopify branch), and only then updates the card.
5. **Page**: Open in page sends a private 8-hour signed link to a list of everything pending.
6. **Remind** nudges once, expires old rows and wakes snoozed alerts.
7. **Sync** closes a card when the item changes somewhere else first.

### Setup
Create a Slack app (bot scopes `chat:write`, `chat:write.public`; Interactivity on). Add credentials: Slack API (bot token), Crypto (signing secret), and for the demo Shopify Custom Auth plus a Crypto with the app's client secret. Fill in each lane's settings, run Setup, publish, and set the Request URL to **Slack button click**'s production URL.

### Customisation
Add a kind to **Kinds**, and give callers an `apply_workflow_id`: that workflow gets every decision with `decision`, `final_value` and `reason`.

### Writes to Shopify
Changes the product title or the variant price. Test on a development store first.

## 1. Setup (run once)
Creates the `approvals` table (it keeps an existing one). For the Shopify demo it also subscribes Sync's webhook to product updates.

## 2. Ask
Call this workflow from any other (Execute Workflow, lane ask). Skips an item that already has an open card, saves the row, posts the card and stores where it went. Returns straight away.

## 3. Click (Slack's Request URL)
Checks the signature, age, app, team and approvers before anything else, then the pending row (double clicks stop here). Edit and Reject open a modal straight away; the decisions go to Apply.

## 4. Apply
Runs your apply workflow, or the demo Shopify branch (title or price), after checking the live value still matches. Only a change that landed updates the card; a failure keeps the buttons and replies in the thread.

## 5. Page
The page behind Open in page. The GET checks the signed link and lists everything pending; its buttons post back with the same signature and go through Apply.

## 6. Remind (daily 09:00)
One thread nudge after `remind_after_hours`, expiry after `expire_after_days`, snoozed alerts back with their buttons. Nothing is ever applied here.

## 7. Sync
Keeps cards in step with the source of truth. *Close approval* (any workflow) or Shopify's product update webhook closes open cards whose value changed somewhere else.

nodes.notes: Run once. Shopify refuses a second identical subscription, which is fine.

nodes.notes: The one entry point for other workflows (and this one). lane: ask (default), apply or close.

nodes.notes: A workflow can only have one Execute Workflow Trigger that runs, so every call comes in here.

nodes.notes: slack_channel: a channel name (#approvals) or ID. page_button adds Open in page to every card.

nodes.name: Kinds

assignments.name: kinds

nodes.notes: Each kind: approval (Approve, Edit, Reject), alert (one action, Snooze, Ignore) or route (one button per team, Ignore). hint says what the buttons do; large_image shows image_url full width.

nodes.name: Already waiting?
nodes.notes: One open card per item and kind.

nodes.name: Build the card
nodes.notes: Header, Before and After (or the alert fact), optional image and details, a context line, what the buttons do, then the buttons from Kinds.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ channel: $json.channel, text: $json.text, blocks: $json.blocks, unfurl_links: false, unfurl_media: false }) }}

nodes.notes: HTTP rather than the Slack node: raw blocks in, channel and ts back.

nodes.name: Slack button click
nodes.notes: Your Slack app's Interactivity Request URL. Raw Body on, so the signature can be checked.

nodes.name: Read the click
nodes.notes: Handles block_actions (buttons, the snooze menu) and view_submission (the two modals).

nodes.name: Click settings
nodes.notes: Blank slack_app_id or slack_team_id accepts any. approver_ids: Slack user IDs; empty means anyone in the channel.

nodes.name: Sign the request
nodes.notes: Crypto credential: Hmac Secret = your Slack app's Signing Secret.

nodes.name: Signature valid?
nodes.notes: Matches Slack and is under 5 minutes old, so a captured request can't be replayed.

nodes.name: Allowed?
nodes.notes: Your app, your workspace, and an approver.

nodes.name: Say not allowed

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ response_type: 'ephemeral', replace_original: false, text: 'Only approvers can decide these cards.' }) }}

nodes.notes: Private reply to whoever clicked.

nodes.name: Get pending row
nodes.notes: A second click, a Slack retry or a card already decided elsewhere finds nothing.

nodes.name: Answer Slack
nodes.notes: Inside Slack's 3 seconds. An empty 200 closes a modal; errors keep it open.

nodes.name: Open the edit modal
nodes.notes: First Slack call after the click: trigger_id lasts 3 seconds and works once.

nodes.name: Open the reject modal
nodes.notes: Optional reason. It goes to your apply workflow, so the next draft can use it.

nodes.name: Sign a page link
nodes.notes: Signs user|expiry for whoever clicked. Cards outlive links, so the card never carries one.

nodes.name: Reply with the link
nodes.notes: Private reply in the channel, only the clicker sees it.

nodes.name: Mark processing
nodes.notes: Straight away, before the slow part, so a fast second click finds nothing pending.

assignments.name: decision
assignments.value: ={{ ({ edit_submit: 'edit', reject_submit: 'reject' })[$('Check the click').first().json.action] || $('Check the click').first().json.action }}

nodes.notes: Calls this same workflow ({{ $workflow.id }}), so it still works after import.

nodes.notes: From Which lane? (lane apply): row_id, decision, final_value, reason, snooze_hours, user_id, via.

nodes.name: Apply settings
nodes.notes: store_domain is only used by the demo Shopify branch.

nodes.name: Where it applies
nodes.notes: Your workflow gets every decision. The demo kinds write to Shopify on Approve, Edit or Match price.

nodes.name: Run your apply workflow
nodes.notes: Its trigger should accept all data. Return { ok: false, error } (or throw) to keep the card open.

nodes.name: Get Shopify token
nodes.notes: Client credentials grant: a fresh Admin API token for this run. See SETUP.md.

nodes.name: Read the live value
nodes.notes: Someone may have changed it in Shopify since the card was posted.

conditions.leftValue: ={{ (n => n && ($('Plan the decision').first().json.kind === 'price_alert' ? Number(n.price) === Number($('Plan the decision').first().json.current_value) : n.title === $('Plan the decision').first().json.current_value))($json.data?.node) }}

nodes.name: Close the card

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ (p => JSON.stringify({ channel: p.channel, ts: p.ts, text: p.word + ': ' + p.item_label, blocks: ((card, word, note, saved) => { const b = JSON.parse(card || '[]').filter(x => x.type !== 'actions' && x.block_id !== 'approval_hint'); if (b[0] && b[0].type === 'header') b[0] = { type: 'header', text: { type: 'plain_text', text: (b[0].text.text.replace(/ to review$/, '') + ': ' + word).slice(0, 150) } }; if (saved) b.push({ type: 'section', text: { type: 'mrkdwn', text: ('*Saved as*\n' + saved).slice(0, 3000) } }); b.push({ type: 'context', elements: [{ type: 'mrkdwn', text: note }] }); return b; })(p.card, p.word, p.note, p.status === 'edited' ? p.final_value : '') }))($('Plan the decision').first().json) }}
